metadata.title: The Legal Briefing Isn't a News Digest.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: what does Claude actually mean by a 'legal briefing' — a news digest, or something else? Lands the carry-out that the briefing is a scan of your own email, calendar, and contracts, run through whichever of three fixed modes the moment calls for.
metadata.anchor_pair: N/A — source is skill-teardown format (anatomy -> pipeline -> constraint -> verdict), no anchor structure to preserve

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes a legal briefing means outside news, delivered each morning. It doesn't. It's a scan of your own email, calendar, and contracts — organized around what's actually happening in your work.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Can Claude email me legal news every morning?', hesitates on 'news', corrects to 'briefings'

props.text:

email me
legal news
every morning?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('news' -> 'briefings') is visible on a late frame.

beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a folder
beats.narration_text: This kind of briefing is built from something called a skill — a folder Claude reads before it works. Inside is one file, written in plain language, that spells out exactly what counts as a briefing here. Claude reads the file, then follows it. The file is the whole program.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder icon opening to reveal SKILL.md, references/, scripts/; SKILL.md highlighted

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder opens on cream to reveal three items: SKILL.md (highlighted in crimson), a references/ folder, a scripts/ folder. A caption below reads 'Claude reads it, then follows it.'

beats.narration_text: The steps run in order: read the file, work through each step exactly as written, then return the result. Nothing runs out of sequence unless a step itself says so.

shot.new_visual_element: Three-phase pipeline: Read SKILL.md -> Execute steps in order -> Return result

production_viz.label: Input in, output out
production_viz.mechanic: Three cards left to right joined by arrows: 'Read SKILL.md', 'Execute steps in order', 'Return result'. Linear, no branch points drawn.

beats.narration_text: For this skill, there are exactly three situations it covers: a daily scan of legal-relevant items across your email, calendar, and contracts; research on one legal question across your own internal sources; and rapid context when something urgent breaks — a breach, a litigation threat, a regulatory inquiry. Ask it about anything else and there's no mode that covers it.

shot.new_visual_element: Three mode cards: daily scan, topic research, incident response; a boundary line with 'nothing outside this list' beyond it

production_viz.label: Exactly three modes
production_viz.mechanic: Three rows fill in one at a time with a checkmark: 'Daily scan — email, calendar, contracts', 'Topic research — one question, your own sources', 'Incident response — breach, threat, inquiry'. A dashed boundary line beneath the list, with a faint unlabelled field beyond it captioned 'nothing outside this list'.

beats.narration_text: A legal briefing here isn't outside news — it's a scan of what's already in your own email, calendar, and contracts, run through whichever of three modes the moment calls for.

props.quote: A legal briefing here isn't outside news — it's a scan of what's already in your own email, calendar, and contracts, run through whichever of three modes the moment calls for.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Ask Claude: look through my recent emails, calendar, and any contracts I have open, and give me a short briefing — what's legal-relevant this week, organized by how urgent it is. If anything looks like it needs fast attention, put that first. Liam, in for Bear.
